task: Website M2 living subject objects plus I2 subject art in wt-web-v2 (web/v2-1015)
done: Commit 53376131 on web/v2-1015 (not pushed). I2: all 29 subject objects are now versioned public/art/subjects/obj-<name>.v2*.webp. Every file is under 120 KB. 9 objects use the app file byte for byte. The other 20 were remade from the lossless I2 masters with the app's crop, one linear-light LANCZOS resize at q80, at the widest size that fits, so their feet are unchanged. Examples: psychology 1024 to 704 px, agriculture 800 to 576 px, history 989 to 768 px. Versioning matters: the Gate A previews cached older objects at the same unversioned names under a one-year immutable cache. data/subject_art.mjs gains each object's float phase and subject light. M2: SubjectObject.jsx plus new ObjectLife.jsx (client island), ObjectLifeModel.mjs (the app's ObjectLife numbers) and subject-object.css (moved out of brand.css). Objects of 96 px and up float (7.2 s, per-subject phase, shadow 0.86 and 0.65 at the top), tilt toward the mouse, a finger and the scroll (909 px, Flutter springs), catch a masked light band, and on tap play the 420 ms spring and twist, a tick and the 560 ms sparkle. The contact shadow is the app's two ellipses. A flight prop wraps the object in React ViewTransition name subj-<name> (420 ms, back 340 ms), and the object it lands on gives the tap spring and a tick. Finding: the handoff's CSS rotateX(tiltY)/rotateY(-tiltX) is mirrored against the app, because Flutter's perspective entry sends +z away and CSS brings it toward the viewer. The web uses rotateX(-y) rotateY(x) so the touched side presses away as in the app.
